extracted.intended_audience: students and instructors studying public relations/crisis communication and general readers researching Domino's 2009 crisis
extracted.subtask_description: A case-study style summary of Domino's 2009 YouTube food-safety crisis, describing the company's actions and outcomes as a model for corporate crisis communication and reputation-repair efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: "It took Domino’s 48 hours to respond to the video, which caused public criticism on social media."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page highlights a 48-hour delay as noteworthy and linked to public criticism; timeliness of response is framed as critical in managing social-media-driven crises — delays can amplify negative reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate corrective action / accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: "They immediately began taking action firing the two employees the following day."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taking decisive internal action (terminations, removal of implicated staff) is presented as an essential first step to demonstrate accountability to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership visibility and direct public statement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Dominos CEO, Patrick Doyle, released his own YouTube video condemning the former employees actions and announcing warrants had been issued for their arrest."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A visible, leadership-led message (CEO video) that condemns wrongdoing and announces legal/disciplinary steps is shown as a way to signal seriousness and ownership to stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the same platform and timely public response content
rubrics_metrics.description: "The incriminating video was posted on YouTube and went viral... Domino’s CEO ... released his own YouTube video..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responding on the same platform where the incident spread (YouTube) is emphasized — matching medium can reach the affected audience quickly and directly with the company's response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing dedicated communication channels for crisis management
rubrics_metrics.description: "A twitter account, @dpzinfo, was opened... The account launched the YouTube video response and became available to the public’s questions and concerns surrounding the crisis. This account diverted the negative responses and comments from Domino’s main twitter account, @dominos."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating a separate, dedicated account to handle crisis communications and funnel negative comments away from main brand channels is presented as a tactic to organize responses and protect core brand presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement and Q&A availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The dedicated account "became available to the public’s questions and concerns surrounding the crisis."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making a channel available for questions and concerns (active engagement) helps address public sentiment and provides a forum for two-way communication during a crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic reputation-repair campaign with clear objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: "Domino’s dedicated themselves to changing their reputation through, 'The Pizza Turnaround' campaign. The campaign’s objective was to create awareness and strengthen relationships with customers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A named, strategic campaign with explicit objectives (awareness, relationship-building) is shown as the next phase after immediate response — repairing trust requires sustained, objective-driven efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product remedy / substantive corrective measures
rubrics_metrics.description: "The campaign’s objective... by getting new customers interested in trying the new recipe, as well as winning back old customers lost to their competition."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making substantive product changes (new recipe) or other tangible improvements is presented as a corrective measure to change customer attitudes and behaviors, not just messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement of outcomes / effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: "The campaign proved successful, as sales increased by 14% in the first quarter and profits doubled."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use business metrics (sales, profit) to evaluate the effectiveness of reputation-repair efforts; measurable improvements are evidence of campaign success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis preparedness and the risk of being 'caught off guard'
rubrics_metrics.description: "The rate the video was being viewed caught the company off guard."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrative implies the importance of monitoring and preparedness — inability to anticipate or rapidly assess viral escalation leaves the company vulnerable and complicates response.
